question: Why do periodic crystals never have five-fold symmetry?
answer: A repeating pattern needs corners that fit 360° exactly. Triangles, squares and hexagons do this, but a pentagon's 108° doesn't go into 360°, so pentagons always leave a gap or an overlap. That is why no repeating crystal can have five-fold symmetry. Only quasicrystals, whose pattern never repeats, have it.
